• **Altercation **means a noisy argument or disagreement, especially in public. (तकरार)

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

To kill two birds with one stone

options.text: A work which needs tremendous efforts
To achieve two things with a single effort
The weak point in a person

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To achieve two things with a single effort.**

• The idiom "**to kill two birds with one stone**" means to accomplish two tasks with a single action.
 
• It is often used to describe an efficient or practical solution to a problem.

• The idiom can be used in both formal and informal contexts.
 
• So, "**To achieve two things with a single effort**" is the appropriate choice to replace the given idiom.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question:
**Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.**

The dessert was __many sweet__ for my tastes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **too sweet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Many**" in the original sentence should be "**too**" to convey the intended meaning of excessive sweetness.
 
• "**Too**" is used to indicate that something exceeds a desired or appropriate amount.
 
• It is used with adjectives to express that a quality is excessive or beyond what is acceptable or desirable.
 
• In this sentence, "**too sweet**" means that the dessert's sweetness level is higher than what the speaker considers enjoyable or acceptable.
 
• "**Many**" is used to quantify countable nouns, indicating a large number or quantity.
 
• It's used with nouns that can be counted, such as "many apples," "many people," "many books," etc.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Corrected sentence:** *The dessert was too__ sweet for my taste. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__

 
• Option 1, "**too sweetly**", is grammatically incorrect because "sweetly" is an adverb that describes how something is done, not how something tastes.
 
• Option 2, "**more sweeter**", is grammatically incorrect because the comparative form of "sweet" is "sweeter", not "more sweeter".
